mechanical_metadata_syncs.former_proposed_value: **Compatible choices before and after the slide.** Let H be N×I with two one-handles h_a,h_b and possibly other disjoint one-handles. Use the orientation of the given four-dimensional handle presentation. Each attachment is orientation-compatible with the oriented base collar, so every closed trade core has orientable rank-three normal bundle and satisfies the normal-bundle hypothesis of [F2]. All feet and the specified slide band are compactly contained off the protected boundary collar. Use the actual k=1 handle-slide definition: after attaching h_b, move one foot of h_a along a thin strip across the interval core of h_b to a parallel of its other endpoint. Its normal D³ travels in the strip coordinates. Denote the resulting handle h_a′. The support is a regular neighborhood of the two handles and the slide strip; no homotopy of the three-dimensional base to a ball is assumed. Choose disjoint replacement arcs B_a,B_b in the base, with fixed product germs at the feet. Let γ_a,γ_b be the corresponding interior core-plus-arc circles in H, pushed to disjoint normal positions. In the slid presentation choose B_a′,B_b′ compatibly with the core-disk push: after identifying the two one-handle stages by the actual slide diffeomorphism, γ_b′ is γ_b and γ_a′ is the framed band sum of γ_a with the signed parallel of γ_b along the slide strip. To obtain these arcs, trace the moved foot back through the slide strip and then along a parallel of B_b, joining the remaining end to B_a inside the foot ball. All segments outside the original handle cores lie in N. Round the two joins in disjoint small balls and put the parallels at different normal positions. The result is an embedded arc after a small relative perturbation in dimension three. The product normal framing is transported by the same strip. This construction proves existence of compatible choices; arbitrary other replacement arc choices are compared by [[lem-one-handle-surgery-replacement-is-independent-of-the-base-arc]].
